An elbow-length-sleeved crew-neck cotton T-shirt, a real plain T-shirt and not a real garment, covered edge to edge in a lightly distressed worn-in print, designed to make the shirt look like the outfit of a teacher in a feminine-styled version. The print is cut to the T-shirt's shape, so the shirt itself looks like the outfit being worn, with the sleeves as the outfit's sleeves. Every panel of the shirt, front, shoulders and sleeves, is a panel of the outfit, showing a tweed jacket with chalk-dusted elbow patches. The print wraps all the way round, the back of the shirt shows the rear of the outfit from the back collar to the hem and along both sleeves. One continuous print of the outfit's cloth covers the shirt from collar band to hem and out to both sleeve hems. The shirt is a standard T-shirt shape with a straight hem across the bottom. The printed top garment continues down the shirt to its straight hem, with at most a belt or sash at the waist. The print is cut exactly to the shirt, neck, shoulders, armholes, sleeves and hem are all covered in the outfit's own fabric. The outfit is laid out on the shirt's own rectangle shape, fully covering it from side seam to side seam. The shirt's sleeves are tailored to end at the elbow, exactly where the outfit's sleeves end. The shirt is solid opaque cotton and every texture and sheen is a printed picture. The print is the garment itself, flat and unfolded over the shirt, in its own cloth and colours. It is the kind of novelty tee that tricks the eye from across a room. It carries enough of the costume to be unmistakable, the headwear's emblem or crest worked into the chest, the lower garment's colours and pattern as a band across the hem and the collar, neckwear and fastenings of the outfit, all in the outfit's own colours. Any printed skin, such as hands, wrists, neck, chest or forearms, is in a flat printed mid-tone brown tanned skin tone.

The outfit is printed across the whole front, over the shoulders and down both sleeves, showing a frock coat with a waistcoat and a stiff collar. Front and back are both fully printed, the back showing how the same outfit looks from behind. The outfit's fabric runs seamlessly over the shoulders and down the sleeves, every part of the shirt in the outfit's own colours and textures. The shirt keeps the outline of an ordinary T-shirt, round neckline, straight side seams, sleeves, and a straight open hem. The shirt is an ordinary T-shirt ending in a straight bottom hem, and the garment printed on it runs straight down the whole shirt to that hem. The outfit's cloth runs unbroken from the collar band across both shoulders and down both sleeves to their hems, so every part of the shirt is outfit cloth. The outfit is laid out on the shirt's own rectangle shape, fully covering it from side seam to side seam. A long-sleeved shirt is used so the outfit's long sleeves fit exactly, printed full length to the shirt's wrist hems. Everything is flat ink on opaque cotton, lace, tulle, fur, feathers, sequins, armour and metal appear as printed patterns. The picture is only the garment, its cloth, seams, buttons and trims laid flat across the whole shirt like a sewing pattern. It also shows printed gloves emerging at the sleeve hems. The printed collar and lapels line up with the shirt's actual neckline. To read as a costume rather than a plain top, it adds the held item or gear of the outfit, shown as a patch or large motif on the chest or a sleeve, the most recognisable props and accessories of the outfit as appliqué pieces and the lower garment's colours and pattern as a band across the hem, bold and large enough to identify the outfit from across a room. Any printed skin, such as hands, wrists, neck, chest or forearms, is in a flat printed mid-tone brown tanned skin tone.

The printed outfit runs from the neckline to the hem and from one sleeve hem to the other, its shoulders on the shirt's shoulder seams, showing a wide embroidered boubou. The back of the shirt is printed just as completely, edge to edge, with the back of the same outfit, its back collar, shoulder blades and the backs of both sleeves. One continuous print of the outfit's cloth covers the shirt from collar band to hem and out to both sleeve hems. It is an ordinary T-shirt in shape, with a straight open hem and sleeves cut to match the outfit's sleeves. The shirt is an ordinary T-shirt ending in a straight bottom hem, and the garment printed on it runs straight down the whole shirt to that hem. The outfit's collar meets the real collar band, its shoulders sit on the real shoulder seams and its sleeves fill the real sleeves, all in one piece of printed cloth. The outfit is laid out on the shirt's own rectangle shape, fully covering it from side seam to side seam. The shirt is a long-sleeved T-shirt matching the outfit's long sleeves, printed with the sleeves and cuffs all the way down to the wrist hems. The sleeve hems are cut at an angle, slanted, pointed or curved, to follow the outfit's own cuffs, and the print follows that edge exactly. Everything is flat ink on opaque cotton, lace, tulle, fur, feathers, sequins, armour and metal appear as printed patterns. The print is the garment itself, flat and unfolded over the shirt, in its own cloth and colours. It also shows a printed collar continuing the outfit up to the neckline and printed cuffs where the sleeves end. It is the kind of novelty tee that tricks the eye from across a room. The tee is clearly a costume tee, not a plain shirt, it shows the outfit's patches, insignia and emblems, the held item or gear of the outfit, shown as a patch or large motif on the chest or a sleeve and the footwear's trim colours as stripes on the cuffs and hem, so anyone can tell at a glance what outfit it stands for. Any printed skin, such as hands, wrists, neck, chest or forearms, is in a flat printed mid-tone brown tanned skin tone.

The printed outfit runs from the neckline to the hem and from one sleeve hem to the other, its shoulders on the shirt's shoulder seams, showing a fitted lace bodice with a sweetheart neckline and a long veil. The back of the shirt is printed just as completely, edge to edge, with the back of the same outfit, its back collar, shoulder blades and the backs of both sleeves. The outfit's own cloth covers the whole shirt as one continuous print, so shoulders, sleeves and body are all in the outfit's colours. It is an ordinary T-shirt in shape, with a straight open hem and sleeves cut to match the outfit's sleeves. The printed top garment continues down the shirt to its straight hem, with at most a belt or sash at the waist. The print is cut exactly to the shirt, neck, shoulders, armholes, sleeves and hem are all covered in the outfit's own fabric. The outfit is stretched to the shirt's own straight-sided shape and fills it completely, so it suits any body size. The shirt is a long-sleeved T-shirt matching the outfit's long sleeves, printed with the sleeves and cuffs all the way down to the wrist hems. Everything is flat ink on opaque cotton, lace, tulle, fur, feathers, sequins, armour and metal appear as printed patterns. The print is the garment itself, flat and unfolded over the shirt, in its own cloth and colours. It may also show flat printed bare skin in a flat printed mid-tone brown tanned skin tone at the throat, chest and forearms where the outfit is open, all as flat ink. Under every lace, net, mesh or see-through area the print shows a flat printed mid-tone brown tanned skin tone, as a printed illusion on solid cotton. The printed collar and lapels line up with the shirt's actual neckline. To read as a costume rather than a plain top, it adds its pockets, flaps and trims, the belt, straps and buckles of the outfit and the lower garment's colours and pattern as a band across the hem, bold and large enough to identify the outfit from across a room. Any printed skin, such as hands, wrists, neck, chest or forearms, is in a flat printed mid-tone brown tanned skin tone.

Every panel of the shirt, front, shoulders and sleeves, is a panel of the outfit, showing a braided tunic with a plume. The back of the shirt is printed just as completely, edge to edge, with the back of the same outfit, its back collar, shoulder blades and the backs of both sleeves. One continuous print of the outfit's cloth covers the shirt from collar band to hem and out to both sleeve hems. The shirt keeps the outline of an ordinary T-shirt, round neckline, straight side seams, sleeves, and a straight open hem. The shirt is an ordinary T-shirt ending in a straight bottom hem, and the garment printed on it runs straight down the whole shirt to that hem. The outfit's cloth runs unbroken from the collar band across both shoulders and down both sleeves to their hems, so every part of the shirt is outfit cloth. The outfit is stretched to the shirt's own straight-sided shape and fills it completely, so it suits any body size. The shirt is a long-sleeved T-shirt matching the outfit's long sleeves, printed with the sleeves and cuffs all the way down to the wrist hems. All textures, transparencies and sheens are printed patterns on solid cotton. The picture is only the garment, its cloth, seams, buttons and trims laid flat across the whole shirt like a sewing pattern. It may also show flat printed skin in a flat printed mid-tone brown tanned skin tone at the neckline, with fine printed body hair where it would naturally show, all as flat ink. The print wraps around the sides so the outfit seems to continue around the body. To read as a costume rather than a plain top, it adds the collar, neckwear and fastenings of the outfit, the held item or gear of the outfit, shown as a patch or large motif on the chest or a sleeve and the most recognisable props and accessories of the outfit as appliqué pieces, bold and large enough to identify the outfit from across a room. Any printed skin, such as hands, wrists, neck, chest or forearms, is in a flat printed mid-tone brown tanned skin tone.

The shirt's neckline is the outfit's collar opening, the shirt's sleeves carry the outfit's sleeves, and the shirt's hem is the outfit's lower edge, showing a vest with gauges. The print wraps all the way round, the back of the shirt shows the rear of the outfit from the back collar to the hem and along both sleeves. The outfit's fabric runs seamlessly over the shoulders and down the sleeves, every part of the shirt in the outfit's own colours and textures. The shirt is a standard T-shirt shape with a straight hem across the bottom. The printed top garment continues down the shirt to its straight hem, with at most a belt or sash at the waist. The outfit's collar meets the real collar band, its shoulders sit on the real shoulder seams and its sleeves fill the real sleeves, all in one piece of printed cloth. The outfit is stretched to the shirt's own straight-sided shape and fills it completely, so it suits any body size. The shirt is cut sleeveless, with armholes where the outfit's sleeves would start. Everything is flat ink on opaque cotton, lace, tulle, fur, feathers, sequins, armour and metal appear as printed patterns. Only the outfit's fabric, trims and fastenings are pictured, spread across the entire shirt as a continuous pattern. The illusion is purely flat and two-dimensional, with no real fabric, buttons or pockets beyond the print. It carries enough of the costume to be unmistakable, its pockets, flaps and trims, the belt, straps and buckles of the outfit and the most recognisable props and accessories of the outfit as appliqué pieces, all in the outfit's own colours. Any printed skin, such as hands, wrists, neck, chest or forearms, is in a flat printed mid-tone brown tanned skin tone.
